meta.title: Why Focus Feels Harder: The Cognitive Friction Trap
meta.description: Moving beyond decision fatigue to explore 'Cognitive Friction'—why our brains are failing under the weight of constant context switching, not just choice overload.

scenes.title: The Friction Problem
scenes.say: We blame our lack of focus on having too many choices, but the real culprit is 'Cognitive Friction'—the hidden cost of switching contexts.

scenes.text:
It's not the choice,
It's the context tax.
scenes.say: Every time you switch between a browser tab, a chat notification, and a document, your brain incurs a 'switching tax' that lingers long after you move on.
Studies show it takes over twenty minutes to fully re-engage with a task after an interruption. We aren't just choosing; we are constantly restarting.

chapters.title: The Neural Cost of Context Switching

scenes.title: The Attentional Residue
scenes.say: When you jump from task to task, your brain leaves behind 'attentional residue'—bits of focus stuck on the previous task, making the current one harder.

scenes.text: The brain does not multitask; it performs rapid serial tasking.
scenes.say: The brain is not designed to juggle. It is simply paying a massive metabolic price to switch contexts at high speed.

scenes.text:
Your focus isn't leaking.
It's being fragmented.
scenes.say: This fragmentation is why focus feels impossible. You aren't losing energy to decisions; you are losing it to constant mental re-calibration.

scenes.title: Building Cognitive Barriers
scenes.say: To reclaim focus, we must stop reducing choices and start increasing 'cognitive friction' for distractions.
Create physical or digital barriers that make distraction harder to access, forcing your brain to stay in one lane for longer periods.

scenes.text:
Design for focus,
Not for speed.
scenes.say: Stop optimizing for efficiency and start optimizing for continuity. Protect your state of flow like a physical perimeter.
The secret to focus isn't choosing better; it's choosing to stay put. Protect your mental continuity today.
